entities.summary: Agatha, wife of Edward the Exile, played a pivotal role in shaping the medieval English monarchy and its relationships with Scotland and the Holy Roman Empire. Born around 1100, Agatha was married to Edward, a claimant to the English throne, and mother of Edgar Ætheling, Saint Margaret of Scotland, and Cristina. Her ancestry remains unclear, sparking speculation among historians. As a member of the Exile family, Agatha's influence extended to the Scottish throne, with her son Edgar Ætheling eventually becoming King of Scotland. Agatha's legacy can be seen in the eventual coronation of her daughter Saint Margaret of Scotland, who would go on to become a patron saint of Scotland. This complex web of family connections and alliances highlights the intricate nature of medieval politics and the ongoing struggle for power in the region. Agatha's existence serves as a reminder of the often-overlooked female figures who played crucial roles in shaping the course of history.
